notes: Evanston Fair Workweek Ordinance 24-O-23 (City Code ch. 3-34), effective Jan. 1, 2024: covered employers have 100+ employees globally in covered industries (retail, hospitality, warehouse, manufacturing, building services); restaurants need 30+ locations and 200+ employees globally; franchisees of networks with 30+ locations are covered. Employees: 2+ hours/week in Evanston.

Predictability pay (§ 3-34-5(B)): per shift the employer adds/subtracts hours, moves, cancels, or adds: with <14 days but >=24 h notice, 1 h; with <24 h notice, min(4, hours in the scheduled shift) when hours are cancelled or reduced, 1 h for all other changes. Paid at the regular rate. Employees may decline hours added with <14 days' notice (§ 3-34-5(A)).

Exceptions (§ 3-34-5(D)): emergencies (with $2/h hazard pay if extra hours are required); mutually agreed shift trades or coverage arrangements between employees; employee-requested changes confirmed in writing (incl. sick leave); documented discipline; self-scheduling. Unlike Chicago there is no exemption for employer-proposed changes the employee agrees to. 'Writing' includes email and text message (definitions). On-call employees paid for on-call time are not owed predictability pay when called in (FAQ Q11).
Right to rest (§ 3-34-7): 1.5x only for the hours worked within 11 h of the previous shift (no premium_applies_to='shift').

params.exemption_note: Exempt only for "a mutually agreed upon shift trade or coverage arrangement between Employees" or an employee-requested change "confirmed in writing"; an employer-requested call-in owes predictability pay even if accepted.

rules.summary: Evanston (100+ employees globally, retail and other industries): inside 14 days, 1 hour at the regular rate per added, moved or changed shift; cuts/cancellations with <24 h notice pay 4 hours or the scheduled shift length, whichever is less.

citation.title: Evanston Ordinance 24-O-23 (as amended), City Code § 3-34-5 — Compensation for schedule changes
citation.excerpt: With less than 24 hours to the Employee: (i) four hours or the number of hours in the Employee's scheduled Shift, whichever is less, when hours are canceled or reduced; (ii) one hour

rules.summary: Employees may decline hours within 11 hours of their last shift; if they agree in writing, those hours are paid at 1.5x the regular rate.

citation.title: Evanston City Code § 3-34-7 — Right to rest (Ord. 24-O-23)
citation.excerpt: An Employee who agrees in writing to work hours described in this Section shall be compensated at one-and-a-half (1.5) times the Employee's regular rate of pay for any hours worked less than 11 hours
